free_tier.stated: Storage and egress are whatever your VPS/host allows. No provider quota exists — the cost moves to the host's bandwidth allowance.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: You pay the host. IPFS docs recommend putting a CDN like Cloudflare in front of the gateway and setting Cache-Control/ETag/X-Ipfs-Roots for cacheability — which is the one genuinely correct architectural move in this slot, but it is Cloudflare's free egress you are relying on, not IPFS's.

tooling: Kubo (go-ipfs), Rainbow (github.com/ipfs/rainbow), Someguy for delegated routing, Helia in-browser; rclone can talk to the Kubo RPC API via a webdav/MFS shim but there is no first-class rclone backend.
chaining: Does not multiply free storage — it only re-serves content you already paid to pin. Combined with a free pinning service it can turn 5 GB of free pinning into unmetered-looking reads, but only for 5 GB of content.
limits_note: Bandwidth of the VPS; DHT lookup latency on cold CIDs; no excess-use protection by default ('Unlike ipfs.io, a self-hosted gateway has no abuse protection by default').

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: This is the honest answer to 'does self-hosting change the economics?': it changes *who* meters you, not *whether* you are metered. It cannot manufacture 500 GB–1 TiB/day of free transit; it just moves the bill to the VPS or CDN.
